:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $\mathbf{a}=\langle k,2,1 \rangle,$ $\mathbf{b}=\langle -2,-1,1 \rangle,$ and $\mathbf{c}=\langle -1,1,2 \rangle$ are coplanar.
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}k & 2 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k(-1\cdot 2-1\cdot 1)-2(-2\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot 1)+(-2\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot (-1)) \\  & =-3k+6-3 \\  & =-3k+3.\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ -3k+3 & =0 \\ k & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=1$.

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $a = ⟨k, 1, 1⟩$, $b = ⟨5, 0, 4⟩$, and $c = ⟨6, 2, 5⟩$ are coplanar.
Find $t$ given that the vectors $p = ⟨3, t, t⟩$, $q = ⟨1, 3, 1⟩$, and $r = ⟨1, 1, 3⟩$ are coplanar.
Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨k,1,4⟩,$ $b=⟨8,0,3⟩,$ and $c=⟨3,1,1⟩$ are coplanar.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}k & 1 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}8 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|+4\cdot |\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k(0\cdot 1-1\cdot 3)-(8\cdot 1-3\cdot 3)+4(8\cdot 1-3\cdot 0) \\  & =-3k+1+32 \\  & =33-3k \\  & =3(11-k).\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 3(11-k) & =0 \\ 11-k & =0 \\ k & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=11.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find $t$ given that the vectors $p=⟨t,t,1⟩,$ $q=⟨3,2,6⟩,$ and $r=⟨3,4,0⟩$ are coplanar.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =|\begin{aligned}t & t & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 6 \\ 3 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =t\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}|-t\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =t(2\cdot 0-4\cdot 6)-t(3\cdot 0-3\cdot 6)+(3\cdot 4-3\cdot 2) \\  & =-24t+18t+6 \\  & =-6t+6 \\  & =6(1-t).\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =0 \\ 6(1-t) & =0 \\ 1-t & =0 \\ t & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=1.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find $t$ given that the vectors $a=⟨3,-1,7⟩,$ $b=⟨t,4,t⟩,$ and $c=⟨2,6,8⟩$ are coplanar.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 7 \\ t & 4 & t \\ 2 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & t \\ 6 & 8\end{aligned}|-(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}t & t \\ 2 & 8\end{aligned}|+7\cdot |\begin{aligned}t & 4 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(4\cdot 8-6\cdot t)+(t\cdot 8-2\cdot t)+7(t\cdot 6-2\cdot 4) \\  & =96-18t+8t-2t+42t-56 \\  & =30t+40 \\  & =10(3t+4).\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 10(3t+4) & =0 \\ 3t+4 & =0 \\ t & =-\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=-\frac{4}{3}.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors  $p=⟨0,-1,-{k}^{2}⟩,q=⟨2,4,8⟩$ and $r=⟨-1,-1,5⟩$ are coplanar.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & -{k}^{2} \\ 2 & 4 & 8 \\ -1 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 8 \\ -1 & 5\end{aligned}|-(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 8 \\ -1 & 5\end{aligned}|+(-{k}^{2})\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =0+(2\cdot 5-(-1)\cdot 8)-{k}^{2}(2\cdot (-1)-(-1)\cdot 4) \\  & =18-2{k}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =0 \\ 18-2{k}^{2} & =0 \\ 2{k}^{2} & =18 \\ {k}^{2} & =9 \\ k & =\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=-3$ or $k=3.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:

$k=${{field-1}}
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -3 \\ -1 & k & 2 \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot |\begin{aligned}k & 2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}|+(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & k \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2(k\cdot 4-(-2)\cdot 2)-((-1)\cdot 4-3\cdot 2)-3((-1)\cdot (-2)-3\cdot k) \\  & =-8k-8+10-6+9k \\  & =k-4.\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ k-4 & =0 \\ k & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=4.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:

$k=${{field-1}}
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & k \\ 1 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}|-0\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}|+k\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(4\cdot 5-3\cdot 2)+0+k(1\cdot 2-4\cdot 0) \\  & =2(20-6)+2k \\  & =28+2k\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =0 \\ 28+2k & =0 \\ 2k & =-28 \\ k & =-14\end{aligned}

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=-14.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨1,3,0⟩$, $b=⟨0,4,2⟩$, and $c=⟨2,k,5⟩$ are coplanar.

$k=${{field-1}}
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
a\cdot (b\times c)=|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & k & 5\end{aligned}|
$$

$$
\begin{aligned} & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ k & 5\end{aligned}|-3\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =(4\cdot 5-2\cdot k)-3(0\cdot 5-2\cdot 2)=(20-2k)+12 \\  & =32-2k\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 32-2k & =0 \\ -2k & =-32 \\ k & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=16.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:

$$

$k=${{field-1}}
$\,$
and

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}4 & {k}^{2} & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|-{k}^{2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(5\cdot 0-3\cdot 1)-{k}^{2}(1\cdot 0-3\cdot 2)+2(1\cdot 1-5\cdot 2) \\  & =4(-3)-{k}^{2}(0-6)+2(1-10) \\  & =-12+6{k}^{2}-18 \\  & =6{k}^{2}-30\end{aligned}

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨k,2,2⟩$, $b=⟨3,0,2⟩$ and $c=⟨4,1,3⟩$ are coplanar.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}k & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k(0\cdot 3-1\cdot 2)-2(3\cdot 3-4\cdot 2)+2(3\cdot 1-4\cdot 0) \\  & =-2k-2+6 \\  & =-2k+4.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find $t$ given that the vectors $p=⟨0,3,6⟩$, $q=⟨t,t,2⟩$, and $r=⟨-1,2,7⟩$ are coplanar.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & 6 \\ t & t & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot |\begin{aligned}t & 2 \\ 2 & 7\end{aligned}|-3\cdot |\begin{aligned}t & 2 \\ -1 & 7\end{aligned}|+6\cdot |\begin{aligned}t & t \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =0-3(t\cdot 7-(-1)\cdot 2)+6(t\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot t) \\  & =-21t-6+12t+6t \\  & =-3t-6.\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =0 \\ -3t-6 & =0 \\ -3t & =6 \\ t & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=-2.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find $t$ given that the vectors $p=⟨t,1,t⟩$, $q=⟨2,-1,-1⟩$, and $r=⟨3,0,1⟩$ are coplanar.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =|\begin{aligned}t & 1 & t \\ 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =t\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|+t\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =t((-1)\cdot 1-0\cdot (-1))-(2\cdot 1-3\cdot (-1))+t(2\cdot 0-3\cdot (-1)) \\  & =-t-5+3t \\  & =2t-5.\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =0 \\ 2t-5 & =0 \\ 2t & =5 \\ t & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=\frac{5}{2}.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨8,4,6⟩,$ $b=⟨8,-4,5⟩,$ and $c=⟨0,2,k⟩$ are coplanar.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 6 \\ 8 & -4 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =8\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 \\ 2 & k\end{aligned}|-4\cdot |\begin{aligned}8 & 5 \\ 0 & k\end{aligned}|+6\cdot |\begin{aligned}8 & -4 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =8(-4\cdot k-2\cdot 5)-4(8\cdot k-0\cdot 5)+6(8\cdot 2-0\cdot (-4)) \\  & =-32k-80-32k+96 \\  & =16-64k \\  & =16(1-4k).\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 16(1-4k) & =0 \\ 1-4k & =0 \\ k & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=\frac{1}{4}.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Find $k$ given that the vectors $x=⟨{k}^{2},-2,5⟩$, $y=⟨1,3,4⟩$, and $z=⟨0,-1,2⟩$ are coplanar.

**In ascending order:** $\,$

$k=${{field-1}}
$\,$
and
$\,$
$k=${{field-2}}
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =|\begin{aligned}{k}^{2} & -2 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & ={k}^{2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|-(-2)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|+5\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & ={k}^{2}(3\cdot 2-4\cdot (-1))+2(1\cdot 2-4\cdot 0)+5(1\cdot -1-3\cdot 0) \\  & ={k}^{2}(6+4)+2(2)+5(-1) \\  & =10{k}^{2}+4-5 \\  & =10{k}^{2}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =0 \\ 10{k}^{2}-1 & =0 \\ 10{k}^{2} & =1 \\ {k}^{2} & =\frac{1}{10} \\ k & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{10}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if 
$k=-\sqrt{\frac{1}{10}}$ or $k=\sqrt{\frac{1}{10}}.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨{k}^{2},7,4⟩,$ $b=⟨6,7,4⟩,$ and $c=⟨3,0,2⟩$ are coplanar.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}{k}^{2} & 7 & 4 \\ 6 & 7 & 4 \\ 3 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & ={k}^{2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|-7\cdot |\begin{aligned}6 & 4 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}|+4\cdot |\begin{aligned}6 & 7 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & ={k}^{2}(7\cdot 2-0\cdot 4)-7(6\cdot 2-3\cdot 4)+4(6\cdot 0-3\cdot 7) \\  & =14{k}^{2}+0-84 \\  & =14{k}^{2}-84 \\  & =14({k}^{2}-6).\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 14({k}^{2}-6) & =0 \\ {k}^{2}-6 & =0 \\ {k}^{2} & =6 \\ k & =\pm \sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=-\sqrt{6}$ or $k=\sqrt{6}.$
